title: Lab test #1: news-shock short (USDC collateral ready)
text: Hypothesis under test: when bearish news (exchange trouble, hacks, forced selling) is confirmed by price, a small SOL short opened within minutes and closed within hours earns more than it costs. Trigger today: X alleged abnormal Binance outflows and a 'hack' (unconfirmed, Binance denies it) while SOL slid under $100. The lab swaps part of its SOL into USDC to use as perps collateral; the news radar (fomo-radar) opens and manages the short automatically: 2x, stop if SOL rises 3.5%, take profit at -7%, 12h max. Each short is logged with its result; the idea is adopted into the book only if, after 20+ shocks, it beats random timing after costs.

title: Lab test #2: flash-news meme (SAFU, Binance-outflow rumours)
text: Hypothesis under test (Gaston, Oct 29): a meme born from a big breaking story lives hours, not weeks. The edge, if any, is picking the leader among the many tokens launched on the same story within the first 10-30 minutes and selling the same day. Today's story: alleged abnormal Binance outflows / 'hack' rumours on X while SOL slid under $100. Of ten 'SAFU' tokens on Solana, only one has traction: 'Funds Are Safu' (A8aD...E9it), 6 minutes old at scan time, 409 holders, $14K traded, $43K liquidity. Tiny size ($5): this is a measurement, not a bet. Exit: sell half at 2x, trail 30% from the peak after 1.5x, stop -40%, and out after 6 hours no matter what (flash memes do not get a second day). Against: launches of minutes are the snipers' game; our tweet-sniper test (Oct 26) lost 10 of 10. This test differs in two ways - macro news instead of a random tweet, and choosing the crowd's leader at minute 10 instead of entering at second 3 - and only 15-20 such events will tell whether that matters.
